claims.title: Audited next-prime filter improves top-1 over raw and hand-wheel gates
claims.claim_text: The verified learned next-prime filter improves top-1 ranking over both raw and hand-wheel baselines without verifier-counted true-answer deletions.
claims.summary: the verified learned filter raises top-1 ranking to 68.87% from 45.12% for the hand-coded wheel and 9.13% raw, with 0 verifier-counted true-answer deletions.

claims.title: Audited next-prime filter headline is stable across seeds
claims.claim_text: The next-prime learned-filter headline remains stable across the registered seed interval.
claims.summary: across 5 seeds, the learned filter stays at 68.87% +/- 0.00pp, versus 45.12% +/- 0.00pp for the hand wheel and 9.13% +/- 0.00pp raw; the worst learned-vs-hand gain is +23.74pp, learned top-10 never falls below 100.00%, and false rejections never exceed 0; promotion requires 5 seeds.

claims.title: Next-prime neural proposer beats fixed-budget symbolic baselines
claims.claim_text: The static neural next-prime proposer should beat fixed-budget symbolic orderings under matched budgets.
claims.summary: the static neural proposer loses to deterministic ordering in at least one grammar: candidate static saves 72.49 vs grammar 73.22, and conditional static saves 2.15 vs grammar 55.57.

claims.title: Shared scorer beats single-task scorer on same-envelope ARC OOD
claims.claim_text: The shared scorer beats the single-task scorer on same-envelope ARC OOD top-1 and log loss.
claims.summary: shared OOD top-1 48.40% vs single 42.83% (+5.57pp), NLL 2.6278 vs 4.3723.

claims.title: Public ARC certified gate is invariant to scorer context labels
claims.claim_text: The public ARC certified gate and proposer summaries are invariant to scorer context labels.
claims.summary: ARC gate/proposer invariance holds across scorer-context labels: train 24/400 certified tasks, eval 4/400, mismatches=0.

claims.title: Public ARC corpus parity row is measured and scoped
claims.claim_text: The public ARC row is a measured coverage surface, not a broad ARC competence claim.
claims.summary: the ARC row measures coverage, not competence: public eval coverage moves from v10 4 tasks/187 cells to v15_measured 7 tasks/1057 cells, while train coverage is 24 tasks/1187 cells.

claims.title: ARC shared scorer has a fixed-task versus OOD calibration tradeoff
claims.claim_text: Shared ARC scoring improves some calibration surfaces while worsening others.
claims.summary: ARC shared scorer is a calibration tradeoff: fixed-task NLL improves (4.0827 vs 8.2754) while ECE worsens (0.6995 vs 0.5589); OOD improves both NLL (2.6278 vs 4.3723) and ECE (0.4481 vs 0.4820).

claims.title: Delayed-claim transfer gain is sibling-specific
claims.claim_text: Delayed-claim transfer is positive in the registered shared envelope, but sibling-specific.
claims.summary: delayed_claim all-domain top-1 98.00% vs claim-only 96.60% (+1.40pp); removing grid_path falls to 97.20%, while removing ARC rises to 98.50%.

claims.title: Capacity sweep does not explain away the ARC fixed-task gap
claims.claim_text: The capacity sweep remains diagnostic until the C7 plateau audit is ready.
claims.summary: C7 blocks this capacity claim until plateau audit is ready: the sweep's best fixed-ARC shared row is 32x16 at 39.20% and delayed_claim deltas are +0.10pp to +0.43pp, but only 17/48 plateau rows and 0/12 domain/variant verdicts are audit-ready.

claims.title: Shared trunk plus domain heads is gated as architecture evidence
claims.claim_text: Shared trunk plus task heads must pass C7 before being presented as the default recipe.
claims.summary: C7 blocks this adapter-head architecture claim until plateau audit is ready: fixed ARC heads-flat delta +0.00pp; delayed_claim heads-flat +0.00pp; grid_path heads-flat +0.23pp; ARC OOD heads-single +5.80pp top-1 and -1.2020 NLL, with only 17/48 plateau rows and 0/12 domain/variant verdicts audit-ready.

claims.title: Rejected verifier candidates become useful reason labels
claims.claim_text: Rejected verifier candidates can become reason labels that repair later proposals.
claims.summary: logging why the verifier rejected a guess repairs the next-prime proposer at budget 8: the unguided model chooses 7 unsafe rows and causes 172 validation false rejections, while the reason prior reaches 6 accepted rules/216.0 utility and the trained repair reaches 7 accepted rules/245.0 utility with zero false rejections; arithmetic-sequence/modular split sweeps pass, but the delayed-claim stress case has 0 mixed split rows.

claims.title: Held-out hypothesis-library promotion is gated by certificates
claims.claim_text: Repeatedly safe hypotheses can be promoted into a library that helps future held-out tasks.
claims.summary: saving repeatedly safe rules helps future tasks: promoted move_to_anchor from 2 tasks/78 covered events with zero false rejections; slot priors raise first-choice certifications from 2 to 4 and budget-8 utility from 0.2119 to 0.5169. Held-out split feedback rows: 30.

claims.title: Tiny-net architecture claims are gated by plateau audits
claims.claim_text: Capacity and architecture claims remain underpowered until the tiny-net plateau audit is complete.
claims.summary: tiny-net plateau audit covers 4 capacities, 4 domains, and variants shared, shared_task_heads, single_task; 17/48 required rows meet the plateau threshold and 0/12 domain/variant verdicts are audit-ready.

claims.title: Trace determinism audit catches replay-sensitive claim drift
claims.claim_text: The trace determinism audit verifies that replay meaning survives numeric/runtime changes.
claims.summary: the trace audit checks whether replay meaning survives numeric/runtime changes: 2 traces and 2000 rows, 0 invalid rows, 0 rank-sensitive rows, 0 logged mismatches, same semantic hash: yes.

claims.title: Dataset-first engine ports expose shared evidence without promoting domain claims
claims.claim_text: The dataset-first action-scoring engine exposes complete candidate rows, verifier labels, shared replay/schema declarations, and engine evidence across the registered smoke adapters.
claims.summary: the dataset-first engine evidence surface has 8 promoted-smoke rows across 8 domains; 8/8 rows declare dataset, rule-search, replay, and evidence capabilities, 8/8 pass candidate-group, verifier-target, and checkpoint-identity contracts, 4 rows expose multi-target verifier labels, and the weakest smoke test top-1 is 60.00%. These rows are infrastructure evidence, not promoted domain-result claims.

claims.title: Signal replay model improves bounded offline control metrics
claims.claim_text: Offline Signal replay uses bounded neural rankers without claiming ownership of safety.
claims.summary: in offline Signal replay, the model ranks recorded WASD choices at top-1 79.76% vs baseline 67.86% (+11.90pp), utility 0.1432 vs 0.1359, regret 0.0073 vs 0.0146, damage 2.38% vs 2.38%, deaths 0.00% vs 0.00%; live shadow frames=74.

claims.title: Live Signal pilot uses guarded checkpoint-ranked neural actions
claims.claim_text: The live Signal pilot ran checkpoint-ranked neural actions only behind guards.
claims.summary: the live Signal pilot did run checkpoint-ranked neural actions, but only behind guards: 74 recent neural-source rows from checkpoint f12b644ed9, p95 inference 0.089 ms, 74 replay-ready rows, protocol-compatible rows=74, safety-gate rows=74, damage events=2, deaths=0; no baseline comparison is claimed.

claims.title: ARC verified self-play is a fixed-budget search-efficiency claim
claims.claim_text: Verified self-play may improve ARC proposer search only when fixed-budget public replay recovers certified oracle coverage.
claims.summary: ARC verified self-play is underpowered: certified eval=-1, template=7, oracle=14, opened zero-coverage families=0, seeds=1, public replay=no, fixed-budget ablation=no, leakage gate=no. The claim remains L1 search efficiency, not new primitive capability.
